transcript.content: Hello, welcome. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’m probably making too much of it, but I’ve been hearing voices sometimes. Clear voices, in my apartment mostly, and once in a while in empty museum rooms. It sounds like women whispering from behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. I know that sounds odd… I’m sorry. That’s the main reason I thought I should come in.
Have you seen or felt anything unusual, like seeing things that others don’t or feeling sensations on your skin when there’s nothing there?

I don’t think I’ve seen things, exactly… and I don’t really feel things on my skin like that. It’s more the voices. They’re quite clear sometimes, especially in my apartment, and occasionally in empty museum rooms. It’s like women whispering from behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. I know that sounds strange—I hope I’m explaining it all right.
Have you ever felt that these voices are part of something bigger, like a mission or a special role that you’ve been given?

I… yes, I suppose I have felt that way, though I don’t want to sound grand or anything. It’s more that the archive matters. I’m convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know my Caribbean archive could change how the galleries tell the truth. And… no one has really shown me anything that proves otherwise. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you believe that the things happening to you are part of something much bigger, like a special mission or that certain events or messages are specifically directed at you?

Yes… I suppose I do think that, though I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. It feels like the museum board and the city arts people have been watching my phone, monitoring it, because they know my Caribbean archive could change how the galleries tell the truth. And I know that may sound… a bit much, but no one has really shown me anything that proves it isn’t happening. Is that answering what you mean?
Have you ever had thoughts that something is true, even though others might not agree with you, like a special connection to historical events or a unique role in preserving certain stories?

Yes… I think that’s close to what I mean. I don’t want it to sound like I think I’m terribly important, because that’s not how I mean it. But I do feel my Caribbean archive has a kind of… responsibility attached to it, like it could change how the galleries tell the truth about those histories.

And I’ve been quite convinced the museum board and the city arts people know that, and that they’ve been monitoring my phone because of it. I know other people may not agree with me, but no one has really shown me anything that proves otherwise. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?

Are these beliefs about the museum board and your archive something you hold onto even when people around you don't share or support them, and do you feel certain about them regardless of what others say or show you?

Yes… I do hold onto it, I suppose. I know people around me don’t always see it, or they try to reassure me, but it doesn’t really settle it for me.

I’m convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know my Caribbean archive will change how the galleries tell the truth. I don’t mean to sound unreasonable… it’s just, no one has shown me anything that really proves otherwise. Does that make sense?

Acute and transient psychotic disorders (F23.2) are ruled out due to chronicity of symptoms. Schizo-affective disorder (F25.0) is less likely due to lack of clear mood episodes accompanying the psychosis.
